scenario.name: SANS DFIR & Microsoft Sysmon — NTFS $MFT $STANDARD_INFORMATION vs $FILE_NAME Timestomping (Sysmon EventID 2)
scenario.overview: Imagine a bustling coastal shipping port with blue harbor water, stacked colorful steel cargo containers, a towering yellow overhead gantry crane, and a moored cargo ship. Out on the concrete harbor pier, a worker notices a single shipping container whose side inspection hatch was accidentally left unlatched during loading. In this real-world scenario, the intruder approaches the harbor crane inspection pier disguised as a regular visitor, then smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches. The port authority watchtower spots footsteps leaving a supposedly sealed container bay and compares the manifest seal numbers against the pier camera. In this scenario (T1070.006, SANS DFIR & Microsoft Sysmon, NTFS $MFT $STANDARD_INFORMATION vs $FILE_NAME Timestomping (Sysmon EventID 2)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: payload Drop, then user-Mode NtSetInformationFile Timestomping, then offline $MFT $SI < $FN Anomaly. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Payload Drop, then User-Mode NtSetInformationFile Timestomping, then Offline $MFT $SI < $FN Anomaly, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 11 with the documented host and network chain.

Specifically in Step 1, the intruder approaches the harbor crane inspection pier disguised as a regular visitor while everyday visitors and the harbor customs inspector go about their routine. Next, the follow-up artifact MFT Attribute 0x10 ($STANDARD_INFORMATION) Created: 2026-11-03 16:40:12.8491023 UTC runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , MFT Attribute 0x10 , $STANDARD_INFORMATION Created: 2026-11-03 16:40:12.8491023 UTC via Syst so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1070.006 during "Payload Drop & True Creation Timestamp in $MFT $FILE_NAME , 0x30 Attribute , Sysmon EventID 11" , When the dropper creates C:\Windows\System32\winhttp_helper while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1070.006 - Sysmon EventID 2 FileCreateTime Changed)
stages.description: Slipping out through that open container hatch while the yellow gantry crane swings overhead, the stowaway steps straight onto the restricted customs dockyard. Here in Step 2 inside the shipping port, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the sealed bonded export yard. The dropper invokes SetFileTime / NtSetInformationFile(FileBasicInformation) or PowerShell (Get-Item winhttp_helper.dll).CreationTime = "2022-05-07 09:00:00" to blend in with legitimate OS binaries. Sysmon EventID 2 (A process changed a file creation time) immediately logs both the forged CreationUtcTime (2022-05-07) and the true PreviousCreationUtcTime (2026-11-03) (logged in Sysmon Event 2 with EventID=2 , Sysmon FileCreateTime Changed, TargetFilename=C:\Windows\System32\winhttp_helper.dll, ForgedCreationUtcTime=2022-05-07 09:00:00.000, PreviousCreationUtcTime=2026-11-03 16:40:12.849 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes NtSetInformationFile(hFile, &ioStatus, &fileBasicInfo, sizeof, FILE_BASIC_INFORMATION, FileBasicInformation) (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , NtSetInformationFile, hFile, &ioStatus, &fileBasicInfo, sizeof, FILE_BASIC_INFORMATION, File so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1070.006 during "User-Mode NtSetInformationFile Timestomping & Sysmon EventID 2 Detection" , The dropper invokes SetFileTime / NtSetInformationFile, FileBasicInformation or PowerShell , Get-Item winhttp_helper while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Sysmon EventID 2: TargetFilename=C:\Windows\System32\winhttp_helper.dll CreationUtcTime=2022-05-07 09:00:00.000 PreviousCreationUtcTime=2026-11-03 16:40:12.849 runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Sysmon EventID 2: TargetFilename=C:\Windows\System32\winhttp_helper.dll CreationUtcTime=2022 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1070.006 during "User-Mode NtSetInformationFile Timestomping & Sysmon EventID 2 Detection" , The dropper invokes SetFileTime / NtSetInformationFile, FileBasicInformation or PowerShell , Get-Item winhttp_helper while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ NtSetInformationFile(FileBasicInformation) backdating winhttp_helper.dll to 2022-05-07 / ⇠#2 ACK 2) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 ntdll!NtSetInformationFile), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 $STANDARD_INFO vs $FILE_NAME).

stages.title: Stage 3: Offline $MFT $SI < $FN Anomaly & Sub-Second Nanosecond Zeroing Analysis (MFTECmd)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1070.006 - $MFT $STANDARD_INFORMATION vs $FILE_NAME Discrepancy)
stages.description: Now roaming freely outside the sealed steel box, the intruder walks across the shipping port pier and alters manifests bound for the moored cargo ship. In this final step inside the shipping port, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the harbor crane inspection pier in tiny disguised batches until the port authority manifest watch catches the mismatch. Because user-mode Win32/NT APIs only modify the $STANDARD_INFORMATION (0x10) attribute while $FILE_NAME (0x30) is updated strictly by the NTFS kernel driver on file creation/move/rename, parsing C:\$MFT with MFTECmd reveals a classic "$SI < $FN" discrepancy ($SI Created = 2022-05-07 09:00:00.0000000 with zeroed fractional seconds vs $FN Created = 2026-11-03 16:40:12.8491023) (logged in WinEvent Event 94102 with ForensicArtifact=C:\$MFT , Master File Table Entry #94102, StandardInfo0x10=2022-05-07 09:00:00.0000000 , uSecZeros=True, FileName0x30=2026-11-03 16:40:12.8491023 , True Drop Timestamp, AnomalyClassification=$SI < $FN Timestomp + Sub-Second Nanosecond Zeroing so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes MFTECmd.exe -f "C:\$MFT" --csv C:\Forensics --csvf mft_parsed.csv (which Parses or manipulates low-level NTFS Master File Table , $MFT record attributes, comparing the user-modifiable $STANDARD_INFORMATION , 0x10 timesta so that exposes anti-forensic timestomping , NtSetInformationFile · T1070.006 or deleted file activity during "Offline $MFT $SI < $FN Anomaly & Sub-Second Nanosecond Zeroing Analysis , MFTECmd" by proving that the 0x10 creation timestamp was backdated earlier than the immutable 0x30 kernel creation timestamp). Next, the follow-up artifact $SI Created0x10: 2022-05-07 09:00:00.0000000 (Zeroed sub-second nanoseconds) runs (which Parses or manipulates low-level NTFS Master File Table , $MFT record attributes, comparing the user-modifiable $STANDARD_INFORMATION , 0x10 timesta so that exposes anti-forensic timestomping , NtSetInformationFile · T1070.006 or deleted file activity during "Offline $MFT $SI < $FN Anomaly & Sub-Second Nanosecond Zeroing Analysis , MFTECmd" by proving that the 0x10 creation timestamp was backdated earlier than the immutable 0x30 kernel creation timestamp). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ MFTECmd.exe -f C:\$MFT (Entry 94102: Created0x10 < Created0x30 & Sub-Second Zeroing) / ⇠#3 ACK 94102) from Node ③ (#3 ntdll!NtSetInformationFile) to Node ④ (#4 Ntfs.sys Driver ($MFT Record)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 $STANDARD_INFO vs $FILE_NAME).

keySpecs.value: During offline NTFS disk triage, flag any $MFT record in System32 where Created0x10 < Created0x30 or where Created0x10 has exact .0000000 sub-second fractional zeros.
